# Diri Djon Djon Recipe: Plant Based Haitian Black Mushroom Rice

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/diri-djon-djon-recipe/
Category: Recipes
Author: Miriam Delva
Published: 2026-11-09

Learn to make a fully plant based diri djon djon, the Haitian black mushroom rice, with homemade epis, a dark strained broth, and simple tips for buying and storing it safely.


Imagine opening a small bag of dried black mushrooms for the first time. They look like a handful of dark, crinkled leaves, and they smell deep and earthy, almost like a forest after rain. You may have eaten diri djon djon at a wedding or a family gathering and wondered how that pot of rice turned so dark and tasted so rich. This diri djon djon recipe will show you exactly how it happens in your own kitchen.

Some of us grew up watching a mother or aunt pour inky mushroom water into the rice without ever writing anything down. Others are new to Haitian cooking and keep hearing friends talk about black rice. Either way, you are welcome here, and this version is fully plant based, with oil in place of butter and vegetable broth in place of meat stock.

Below you will learn what djon djon is and how to steep and strain it for a dark broth. You will also blend a fresh homemade epis. Then we cover where people look for djon djon around Dallas Fort Worth, how flavored bouillon cubes differ from the real mushrooms, and how to keep leftovers safe.

## The short answer

Diri djon djon is Haitian black rice made by steeping dried djon djon mushrooms in hot water, straining the dark liquid, and cooking long grain rice in it with garlic, onion, herbs, and peas. The mushrooms give the rice its deep gray to black color and an earthy, savory flavor. Our plant based version uses oil, homemade epis, and vegetable broth, so it suits Seventh-day Adventist and vegan tables alike.

- 50 min : Prep time
- 40 min : Cook time
- 6 servings : Makes

The prep time above includes a thirty minute steep for the mushrooms, which is the part that needs patience more than effort. If you prefer, you can steep them in the refrigerator overnight and make the rice the next day. The cook time includes the ten minute rest at the end, and the cooking itself is mostly hands off once the lid goes on.

## What is diri djon djon?

Diri djon djon is a Haitian rice dish cooked in the strained, dark liquid of dried djon djon mushrooms, which gives it its famous color and earthy taste. The word diri means rice in Kreyòl, so the name simply tells you it is rice with djon djon. Writing for Epicurious, Nadege Fleurimond describes it as a welcome sight at Haitian weddings, First Communions, and other celebrations, and as something families also enjoy at ordinary Sunday dinners. It is a dish that says a meal is special without needing any meat at all.

### What is a djon djon mushroom?

A djon djon mushroom is a small, dark mushroom that Haitian cooks dry and later soak to release a black, flavorful liquid. The Epicurious article identifies the prized variety as Psathyrella cf. hymenocephala, the "cf." meaning scientists compare it to that species rather than naming it with full certainty. The same article explains that djon djon is often called a staple of northern Haiti, yet it also grows in other damp, shady places, and the writer's father recalls it growing among weeds and damp trees in their hometown of Torbeck in southern Haiti. It is gathered in the rainy season and there are no formal djon djon farms, which helps explain why it can be hard to find and costly.

## The Shekinah style plant based diri djon djon

This is our own family style version, easy to follow on a busy Friday afternoon. Many versions build flavor with butter, meat, or seafood, but the mushroom broth is savory enough on its own. We season the pot with homemade epis, add a whole scotch bonnet for fragrance rather than heat, and finish with green peas for color.

| Ingredient | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Dried djon djon mushrooms | 1 cup, loosely packed |
| Boiling water for steeping | 3 cups |
| Low sodium vegetable broth | About 1/2 cup, as needed |
| Jasmine or other long grain white rice | 2 cups |
| Olive or canola oil | 2 tablespoons |
| Homemade epis (below) | 1/4 cup |
| Yellow onion, finely chopped | 1 small |
| Fresh thyme | 3 sprigs |
| Whole cloves | 3 |
| Whole scotch bonnet pepper, not cut (optional) | 1 |
| Frozen green peas | 1 cup |
| Salt | About 1 teaspoon, to taste |

### Making the homemade epis

Epis is a blended green seasoning of herbs, garlic, and peppers, and making it fresh takes only a few minutes in a blender. Our version leans on green onion and parsley for brightness and lime juice for a gentle tang. This batch makes more than the quarter cup you need for the rice, so you will have some left for beans or vegetables. Keep the extra in a covered jar in the refrigerator and use it up soon, because fresh garlic and herbs blended with oil are best kept cold rather than left on the counter.

| Epis ingredient | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Green onions, roughly chopped | 4 |
| Fresh flat leaf parsley | 1/2 cup, packed |
| Garlic cloves | 4 |
| Green bell pepper, chopped | 1/2 pepper |
| Fresh thyme leaves | 1 teaspoon |
| Fresh lime juice | 1 tablespoon |
| Olive oil | 2 tablespoons |

### Method

- Steep : Pour boiling water over the djon djon and steep 30 minutes
- Strain : Squeeze the mushrooms and strain the broth through a cloth lined sieve
- Sauté : Cook onion and epis in oil until fragrant
- Simmer : Add rice, 3 cups liquid, thyme, cloves, and salt, then cover on low
- Finish : Fold in peas, rest 10 minutes, and fluff

Place the dried djon djon in a heatproof bowl, pour the boiling water over it, and press the mushrooms under with a spoon. Let them steep for about thirty minutes while you rinse the rice and blend the epis. When the water is very dark, squeeze the mushrooms firmly over the bowl, then pour the liquid through a fine sieve lined with a clean cloth or paper towel to catch any grit.

Measure the dark broth and add enough vegetable broth to make exactly 3 cups. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion for about four minutes until soft. Stir in the epis for a minute or two, then add the rinsed rice and stir until every grain is coated. Keeping the liquid at exactly 3 cups for 2 cups of rice is what keeps the grains separate instead of mushy.

Pour in the 3 cups of djon djon liquid, then add the thyme sprigs, cloves, salt, and the whole scotch bonnet if you are using it. Bring everything to a boil, stir once, then lower the heat as far as it will go and cover the pot tightly. Cook for about eighteen to twenty minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Scatter the frozen peas over the top, cover again, and let the pot rest off the heat for ten minutes before removing the pepper, thyme stems, and cloves and fluffing the rice with a fork.

## Where to buy djon djon and what to look for

### Where can you buy djon djon in the Dallas Fort Worth area?

You can usually find dried djon djon at Latin or Caribbean grocery stores, through small independent sellers in the Haitian community, or from online retailers. The Epicurious article describes people buying it at local Latin stores, from individual sellers, through relatives who bring it back from Haiti, and online. We are not naming specific stores here because stock changes often, so call ahead before you drive across the Metroplex. Asking friends in the Haitian community is often a good way to learn who has a fresh bag.

Expect to pay more than for most dried mushrooms. Epicurious quoted a chef who said a mamit, a three quart container used as a common measure in Haiti, can cost $35 to $50 from a South Florida vendor, and the writer once paid $60 for one in Brooklyn. Look for dark, dry caps with little dust or debris. Store the bag tightly sealed in a cool, dry cupboard.

### Are djon djon bouillon cubes the same as real mushrooms?

No, djon djon flavored bouillon cubes are a seasoning product, not dried djon djon mushrooms, and they cook differently. The Epicurious article notes that some Haitian cooks consider the cubes a decent substitute when the real mushroom is unavailable, while others prefer to avoid them. If you use one, read the label carefully, since some bouillon products contain animal ingredients, and taste before adding salt.

Related: [Diri ak Pwa the Healthy Way](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/diri-ak-pwa-the-healthy-way/)

## Food safety for djon djon and rice

### Is it safe to pick wild mushrooms to make djon djon?

No, you should never eat wild mushrooms you picked yourself unless an expert has identified them. Poison Control warns that many edible mushrooms have poisonous look alikes, that symptoms can be delayed for many hours, and that some mushrooms can seriously damage the liver. Buy dried djon djon from a trusted source and leave foraging to people with real expertise. If you think someone has eaten a wild mushroom, call Poison Control right away at 1 800 222 1222.

Treat the soaking liquid as a perishable ingredient. Use it the same day, or refrigerate it covered if you steep overnight. Freeze any extra broth rather than leaving it on the counter.

Cooked rice deserves the same care. The USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service says to refrigerate perishable food within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when the temperature is above 90°F, and to keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below. FSIS also recommends cooling leftovers quickly in shallow containers, using most cooked leftovers within 3 to 4 days, and reheating them to 165°F. On a hot Texas afternoon, that one hour rule matters for any rice that travels to a church fellowship meal.

**Safe djon djon kitchen**
- Buy djon djon from a trusted seller, never forage it yourself
- Strain the broth through cloth to catch grit
- Refrigerate soak water you are not using right away
- Chill cooked rice within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F
- Store leftovers in shallow containers and eat within 3 to 4 days
- Reheat leftovers to 165°F

## Is diri djon djon healthy?

Diri djon djon can be part of a healthy plate, especially when you cook it with little salt, plenty of vegetables, and some whole grain rice. Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health's Nutrition Source explains that whole grains keep the bran, germ, and endosperm, while milling strips away the bran and germ that carry fiber, B vitamins, and minerals. The same source reports that people who ate two or more servings of brown rice a week had an 11% lower risk of diabetes than those who rarely ate it.

Related: [Pikliz: The Spicy Haitian Slaw That Brightens Every Sabbath Plate](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/pikliz-the-spicy-haitian-slaw/)

## Every good grain is a gift

The food on our tables does not begin in the grocery store. It begins with the Creator who sends rain and brings food out of the ground. The psalmist praises Him for it.

> "He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man: that he may bring forth food out of the earth;" Psalm 104:14, KJV

As Seventh-day Adventists, we see caring for our bodies as part of honoring God. Paul closes a discussion about food and conscience in Corinth with words that lift even a plain meal into worship. When we cook with gratitude and share generously, a pot of black rice becomes a small act of praise.

> "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God." 1 Corinthians 10:31, KJV

## Questions people ask

### Why is my diri djon djon not black enough?

Diri djon djon usually turns out pale when the mushroom liquid is too weak, either from too few mushrooms, too much water, or too short a steep. Squeeze the soaked mushrooms firmly and use the darkest broth possible, topping up with vegetable broth only at the end. Some cooks also blend the soaked mushrooms with their liquid and strain again for a more concentrated broth, a method the Epicurious article describes. Next time, try a longer or overnight steep in the refrigerator.

### Is diri djon djon vegan?

Diri djon djon is not always vegan, because many traditional recipes add butter, meat, or seafood, and some bouillon products contain animal ingredients. The mushrooms, rice, herbs, and peas themselves are all plant foods. Our recipe is fully vegan and Adventist friendly, using oil instead of butter and vegetable broth instead of meat stock. If you are buying it from a restaurant or caterer, ask how it was made.

### Do you eat the djon djon mushrooms?

Most cooks do not eat the djon djon mushrooms, because the treasured part is the dark liquid they release. The Epicurious article explains that the mushrooms are usually discarded after straining, although a cook will occasionally use both the liquid and the mushrooms. Once squeezed well, they have given nearly all their color and flavor to the broth, so compost them if you can.

Related: [Legim Without Meat: A Family Favorite](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/legim-without-meat-a-family-favorite/)

## A word of encouragement

You do not need to be an expert cook to make a meal that blesses others. If your first pot comes out lighter or softer than you hoped, it will still taste of love and effort. God sees the patience it takes to steep, strain, and stir, and nothing done in love is wasted.

# Dis Kòmandman Bondye yo: Kisa yo vle di e èske yo toujou valab jodi a?

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/dis-komandman-bondye-yo/
Category: Bible Answers
Author: Esther Baptiste
Published: 2026-11-09

Yon etid klè an Kreyòl sou Dis Kòmandman Bondye yo nan Egzòd 20, sa Jezi te anseye sou lalwa, ak kijan lagras ak obeyisans mache ansanm nan lavi fanmi w.


Imajine yon aswè lakay ou. Manje a sou dife, televizyon an ap pale pou kont li, epi pitit ou ki nan twazyèm ane antre nan kizin nan ak yon kesyon: "Manman, pwofesè a nan legliz la di Bondye te bay Dis Kòmandman. Kilès yo ye?" Ou kòmanse ak konfyans: pa gen lòt dye, pa fè zidòl, pa pran non Bondye pou ryen, epi memwa w bloke. Si sa rive w, pa wont. Anpil moun ki grandi nan legliz pa ka site Dis Kòmandman Bondye yo san yo pa gade nan Bib la.

Men kesyon an pi gwo pase yon jwèt memwa. Lè ou gade bò wout yo, nan tribinal, oswa nan diskisyon sou entènèt, ou wè moun ap goumen sou Dis Kòmandman yo. Gen moun ki di se yon vye lwa ki pa konsène nou ankò. Gen lòt ki di se chemen pou ou rive nan syèl la. Gen lòt toujou ki pa janm li yo menm, men yo gen yon opinyon fò sou yo.

Nan etid sa a, n ap pran tan nou pou n li Egzòd 20 ansanm, kòmandman pa kòmandman, an Kreyòl ki klè. N ap gade sa Jezi menm te di sou lalwa, kijan lalwa ak lagras mache men nan men, ak poukisa kretyen yo pa toujou konte kòmandman yo menm jan. Epi n ap fini ak kèk etap pratik pou fanmi w ka viv yo chak jou, san pè ak san chay.

## Repons kout la

- 10 : Pawòl Bondye pale ak pwòp vwa li
- 2 : Tab wòch Bondye ekri ak dwèt li
- 2 : Gwo kòmandman Jezi rezime yo

Dis Kòmandman Bondye yo se dis pawòl Bondye te pale sou mòn Sinayi epi li te ekri sou de tab wòch (Egzòd 20:1 rive 17, Egzòd 31:18). Kat premye yo montre nou kijan pou nou renmen Bondye, sis lòt yo montre kijan pou nou renmen pwochen nou. Jezi pa t aboli yo, li te akonpli yo epi li te montre sans yo pi fon. Nou pa sove paske nou obeyi yo; nou obeyi yo paske Bondye sove nou pa lagras.

Konsa, wi, Dis Kòmandman yo toujou valab jodi a, men yo pa yon nechèl pou nou monte rive jwenn Bondye. Yo se tankou yon pòtre karaktè Bondye, epi yon gid pou yon lavi ki gen lanmou ladan l. Rès etid la ap montre ki kote nan Bib la chak pati nan repons sa a soti, epi kijan pou nou viv li lakay nou, nan travay nou, ak nan legliz nou.

## Ki kote Dis Kòmandman yo nan Bib la?

Dis Kòmandman yo nan Bib la parèt de fwa: premye fwa nan Egzòd 20:1 rive 17, lè Bondye pale ak pèp la sou mòn Sinayi, ak dezyèm fwa nan Detewonòm 5:6 rive 21, lè Moyiz repete yo pou yon nouvo jenerasyon. Sa ki fè yo diferan de lòt lwa nan Ansyen Testaman an, se ke Bondye menm te pale yo ak vwa li devan tout pèp la. Apre sa, li te ekri yo li menm sou wòch. Ekriti a di sa byen klè.

> "And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God." Exodus 31:18, KJV

Gade lòd evènman yo nan istwa a, paske li gen yon leson ladan l. Bondye pa t bay pèp la lalwa pandan yo te toujou esklav an Ejip pou di yo: "Obeyi m, epi m ap libere nou." Non, li te libere yo anvan, epi apre sa li te ba yo pawòl li yo. Kòmandman yo kòmanse ak yon fraz ki fè nou sonje sa: Bondye prezante tèt li kòm Seyè ki te fè yo soti nan peyi Lejip, kote yo te esklav (Egzòd 20:2, parafraz an Kreyòl). Lagras vini anvan, lalwa vini apre, tankou yon papa ki sove pitit li anvan li ba l règ lakay la.

- Egzòd 19: Pèp la rive bò mòn Sinayi: Nan twazyèm mwa apre yo fin soti an Ejip, yo kanpe bò mòn nan

- Egzòd 20: Bondye pale Dis Kòmandman yo: Tout pèp la tande vwa Bondye sou mòn nan

- Egzòd 31:18: De tab wòch yo: Bondye bay Moyiz tab yo, ekri ak dwèt li

- Egzòd 32 rive 34: Tab yo kraze, Bondye ekri yo ankò: Apre peche ti bèf lò a, Bondye renouvle akò a sou nouvo tab

- Detewonòm 10:1 rive 5: Tab yo nan lach la: Moyiz mete tab yo anndan lach akò a

## Ki 10 kòmandman Bondye yo, youn pa youn?

Men 10 kòmandman Bondye yo jan yo parèt nan Egzòd 20, rezime an Kreyòl senp. Nan tablo a, nou ekri yo ak pwòp mo nou pou fasilite lekti a; pi ba, kote nou site Bib la mo pou mo, nou di ki vèsyon nou itilize. Nou swiv fason tradisyon refòme, anglikan ak òtodòks yo konte kòmandman yo, kote zidòl se dezyèm kòmandman an. Pita n ap pale de lòt fason kretyen konte yo.

| Nimewo | Sa kòmandman an mande | Egzòd 20 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Pa gen okenn lòt dye devan Bondye | Vèsè 3 |
| 2 | Pa fè ni adore zidòl | Vèsè 4 rive 6 |
| 3 | Pa sèvi ak non Bondye nan move fason | Vèsè 7 |
| 4 | Sonje jou Saba a, setyèm jou a, pou kenbe l sen | Vèsè 8 rive 11 |
| 5 | Onore papa ak manman | Vèsè 12 |
| 6 | Pa touye moun | Vèsè 13 |
| 7 | Pa fè adiltè | Vèsè 14 |
| 8 | Pa vòlè | Vèsè 15 |
| 9 | Pa bay fo temwayaj | Vèsè 16 |
| 10 | Pa anvi sa ki pou lòt moun | Vèsè 17 |

### Kisa kat premye kòmandman yo anseye sou relasyon nou ak Bondye?

Kat premye kòmandman yo anseye nou ke Bondye merite premye plas nan kè nou, nan adorasyon nou, nan pawòl nou, ak nan tan nou. Premye a se fondasyon tout rès la. Si Bondye pa premye, tout lòt bagay ap glise soti nan plas yo. Bib Sen An tradwi l konsa:

> "Ou pa pou gen lòt dye devan M." Egzòd 20:3, Bib Sen An

Jodi a, pi fò nan nou pa gen estati nan lakou nou, men nou tout konnen sa sa ye pou yon bagay pran plas Bondye. Sa ka se lajan, telefòn nan, yon relasyon, menm yon travay nou renmen anpil. Dezyèm kòmandman an ale pi lwen: li entèdi nou fè imaj pou nou adore, paske Bondye vivan an pa ka fèmen nan bwa oswa nan wòch (Egzòd 20:4 rive 6, parafraz). Epi nan menm pasaj la, Bondye pwomèt li montre lanmou li a plizyè milye moun ki renmen l epi ki kenbe kòmandman li yo. Se pa yon Bondye ki ap chache kraze nou, se yon Bondye ki pa vle pataje kè nou ak bagay ki pa ka renmen nou tounen.

Twazyèm kòmandman an pale sou non Bondye (Egzòd 20:7). Se pa sèlman yon kesyon pa fè sèman pou ryen ni pa jire. Lè nou di nou se moun Bondye, nou pote non li, menm jan yon pitit pote non fanmi li nan katye a. Si nou rele tèt nou kretyen epi nou trete moun mal, nou sèvi ak non sa a pou ryen. Kòmandman sa a envite nou viv yon fason ki fè non Papa nou onè.

Katriyèm kòmandman an se sèl ki kòmanse ak mo "sonje," epi li fikse atansyon nou sou setyèm jou semèn nan. Se tankou si Bondye te konnen nou t ap gen tandans bliye l nan mitan tout okipasyon nou. Men pawòl la jan Bib Sen An bay li:

> "Sonje jou Saba a pou kenbe l sen." Egzòd 20:8, Bib Sen An

Kòmandman sa a di klè ke se setyèm jou a ki Saba Seyè a, e li bay rezon an: Bondye te kreye syèl la ak tè a nan sis jou epi li te repoze setyèm jou a (Egzòd 20:11). Nan Bib la, yon jou konte depi solèy kouche rive solèy kouche (Jenèz 1:5, Levitik 23:32), kidonk jou Saba a kòmanse Vandredi lè solèy kouche epi li fini Samdi lè solèy kouche. Nou p ap antre nan tout detay yo isit la, paske nou gen yon etid konplè an Kreyòl sou sijè sa a. Si w vle konprann Saba a depi kreyasyon an rive nan lavi Jezi, li lòt etid sa a lè ou fin li sa a.

Related: [Kisa Bib la di sou Saba a? Jou Saba nan Bib la](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/kisa-bib-la-di-sou-saba-a/)

### Kisa sis dènye kòmandman yo anseye sou relasyon nou ak lòt moun?

Sis dènye kòmandman yo anseye ke renmen Bondye toujou parèt nan fason nou trete moun bò kote nou, kòmanse lakay nou. Senkyèm kòmandman an se pon ant de pati yo, paske paran yo se premye pòtre otorite ak swen timoun yo konnen. Se la tou nou kòmanse aprann respè.

> "Onore papa ou avèk manman ou, pou jou lavi ou yo kapab anpil nan peyi ke SENYÈ a, Bondye ou a te bay ou." Egzòd 20:12, Bib Sen An

Lapòt Pòl fè remake ke se premye kòmandman ki vini ak yon pwomès (Efezyen 6:2). Onore paran pa vle di nou dakò ak yo sou tout bagay, oswa nou kite yo fè nou mal. Li vle di nou respekte yo, nou pale yo byen, epi lè yo vin granmoun, nou okipe yo. Nan kilti ayisyen an, nou konnen byen kisa sa ye pou yon pitit voye kòb lakay pou grann ak granpapa; se yon fason pou viv kòmandman sa a ak men nou.

> "Ou pa pou touye moun." Egzòd 20:13, Bib Sen An

Sizyèm kòmandman an pwoteje lavi, paske chak moun fèt nan imaj Bondye. Jezi te montre ke kòmandman sa a kòmanse nan kè a, lè kòlè ak mepri kòmanse pouse rasin (Matye 5:21 rive 22). Setyèm kòmandman an, ki di pa fè adiltè (Egzòd 20:14), pwoteje maryaj ak fidelite. Jezi te pale de li menm jan, li te montre ke peche a kòmanse nan je ak nan lide, anvan li rive nan kò a (Matye 5:27 rive 28). Pou yon koup marye, kòmandman sa a se tankou yon kloti alantou yon jaden: li pa la pou fèmen lanmou, men pou pwoteje l.

> "Ou pa pou vòlè." Egzòd 20:15, Bib Sen An

Wityèm kòmandman an pa sèlman pou moun ki kase pòt. Li touche fason nou travay, fason nou peye dèt nou, ak fason nou itilize tan patwon nou. Nevyèm kòmandman an pwoteje verite a ak repitasyon lòt moun.

> "Ou pa pou fè fo temwayaj kont vwazen ou." Egzòd 20:16, Bib Sen An

Nan yon epòk kote yon vye rimè ka fè wonn mond lan sou WhatsApp anvan dlo te a fin bouyi, kòmandman sa a pi aktyèl pase jounal maten an. Gaye yon tripotay se tankou louvri yon zòrye plim nan van; ou pa janm ka ranmase tout plim yo ankò. Dizyèm kòmandman an, ki di pa anvi sa ki pou lòt moun (Egzòd 20:17), desann pi fon pase tout lòt yo, paske li jije dezi kè a. Pòl di se kòmandman sa a ki te fè l rekonèt peche nan pwòp kè li (Women 7:7).

## Jezi ak lalwa: èske li te vin aboli Dis Kòmandman yo?

Non, Jezi te di dirèkteman ke li pa t vin aboli lalwa, men li te vin akonpli l. Nan Sèmon sou Mòn nan, li te reponn kesyon sa a menm anvan moun te poze l. Pawòl li yo pa kite plas pou dout.

> "Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil." Matthew 5:17, KJV

Nan vèsè ki swiv yo, Jezi ajoute ke pa gen yon ti pwen, pa gen yon ti mak nan lalwa a ki pral disparèt toutotan syèl la ak tè a la, epi moun ki anseye lòt moun dezobeyi menm pi piti kòmandman yo ap rele pi piti nan wayòm syèl la (Matye 5:18 rive 19, parafraz an Kreyòl). Nan kontèks vèsè sa yo, nou konprann ke "akonpli" pa vle di "fini ak li," tankou yon kontra ki ekspire. Li vle di Jezi te viv lalwa nèt ale, li te montre sans pwofon li, epi li te ranpli l ak lanmou.

Yon jou, yon dòktè lalwa mande Jezi ki kòmandman ki pi gran. Matye di li te poze kesyon an pou l sonde Jezi (Matye 22:35). Se te yon pèlen, men repons Jezi a tounen pi bèl rezime tout lalwa a.

> "Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets." Matthew 22:37 to 40, KJV

Remake ke Jezi pa t mete Dis Kòmandman yo sou kote pou ranplase yo ak lanmou. Li te montre ke lanmou se rasin yo. Pòl di menm bagay la lè li site plizyè nan kòmandman yo epi li di lanmou se akonplisman lalwa (Women 13:8 rive 10). Epi Jezi fè koneksyon an pi pèsonèl toujou nan yon vèsè ki kout anpil.

> "If ye love me, keep my commandments." John 14:15, KJV

Jezi pa di: "Kenbe kòmandman m yo pou m ka renmen nou." Li di: si nou renmen m, n ap kenbe yo. Obeyisans lan se fwi relasyon an, li pa yon pri nou peye pou n achte l.

## Èske Dis Kòmandman yo toujou valab jodi a?

Wi, Dis Kòmandman yo toujou valab jodi a, paske yo montre karaktè Bondye, epi karaktè Bondye pa chanje. Nouvo Testaman an site yo plizyè fwa kòm yon gid pou kretyen yo, pa kòm yon souvni istorik. Jak di ke menm Bondye ki di pa fè adiltè a, se li ki di pa touye moun, e moun ki kase youn koupab devan tout lalwa a (Jak 2:10 rive 11). Jan defini peche kòm dezobeyisans lalwa (1 Jan 3:4). Epi Pòl reponn moun ki ta panse lafwa efase lalwa.

> "Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law." Romans 3:31, KJV

Gen kretyen sensè ki wè sa yon lòt jan. Kèk ladan yo kwè ke Dis Kòmandman yo, kòm yon lis, te fini sou lakwa, e ke kounye a kretyen yo swiv "lalwa Kris la," ki se kòmandman moral Nouvo Testaman an repete. Nou respekte frè ak sè sa yo, epi nou dakò ak yo sou yon pwen enpòtan: pèsonn pa sove pa lalwa. Men lè nou li pasaj yo pi wo a, nou wè Nouvo Testaman an kontinye pale de menm lalwa a, kòmandman pa kòmandman. Pwomès nouvo akò a, se pa ke Bondye ap efase lalwa li, men ke li ap ekri l nan kè nou (Ebre 8:10).

## Lalwa ak lagras: èske nou sove paske nou obeyi?

Non, nou pa sove paske nou obeyi lalwa; nou sove pa lagras Bondye, pa mwayen lafwa nan Jezi, epi obeyisans lan vini apre kòm repons lanmou nou. Lòd sa a enpòtan anpil, paske si nou chanje l, levanjil la tounen yon chay. Pòl eksplike l nan twa vèsè ki merite pou nou aprann pa kè.

> "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them." Ephesians 2:8 to 10, KJV

Gade byen kijan vèsè 8 ak 9 retire tout lògèy: sali a se yon kado, pa yon salè. Men vèsè 10 la fèmen pòt la pou moun ki ta di obeyisans pa enpòtan: Bondye kreye nou nan Kris la pou nou fè bon zèv. Lalwa se tankou yon glas: li montre ou figi w sal, men se dlo ki lave l. Lalwa montre nou peche nou, epi li voye nou kouri jwenn Jezi, ki se sèl ki ka netwaye nou.

Yon deklarasyon kwayans ki pibliye sou lalwa Bondye (kwayans fondamantal nimewo 19, ki rele "The Law of God") rezime sa nan yon fraz kout an Anglè: sali a se "all of grace and not of works," sa vle di tout se lagras, pa zèv, men fwi li se obeyisans a kòmandman yo. Se pou sa nou di: nou kenbe lalwa paske nou sove, pa pou nou sove. Lè yon moun fin resevwa lagras, kenbe kòmandman yo pa tounen yon lis tchèk pou montre Bondye kijan nou bon. Li tounen yon fason pou nou di Bondye mèsi, epi pou nou kite Sentespri a fòme karaktè Jezi nan nou.

## Ki diferans ki genyen ant lalwa moral la ak lwa seremoni yo?

Lalwa moral la se Dis Kòmandman yo, Bondye te ekri yo li menm sou wòch, epi yo toujou valab; lwa seremoni yo se règ sou sakrifis ak rit nan tanp lan ki te montre dwèt sou Jezi, e yo te jwenn akonplisman yo lè Jezi mouri sou lakwa. Konfizyon ant de kategori sa yo lakòz anpil diskisyon pou ryen. Lè yon moun di "Nou pa anba lalwa ankò, nou pa touye mouton ankò," li gen rezon sou mouton yo, men sa pa vle di nou ka vòlè oswa bay manti.

**Lalwa moral ak lwa seremoni**
- Dis Kòmandman yo: Bondye pale yo, li ekri yo sou wòch, yo te mete anndan lach la
- Lwa seremoni yo: Moyiz ekri yo nan yon liv, yo te mete liv la bò kote lach la
- Sakrifis yo te montre dwèt sou Jezi, Ti Mouton Bondye a
- Lè Jezi mouri, sakrifis yo fini; karaktè Bondye pa fini

Bib la li menm fè diferans lan nan fason li trete de kalite lwa sa yo. Tab wòch yo te mete anndan lach akò a (Detewonòm 10:1 rive 5), pandan liv lalwa Moyiz te ekri a te mete bò kote lach la (Detewonòm 31:24 rive 26). Liv Ebre eksplike ke sakrifis bèt yo te sèlman yon lonbraj de sa ki t ap vini, e ke Jezi te ofri tèt li yon fwa pou tout (Ebre 10:1 rive 10). Nan yon atik pou Enstiti Rechèch Biblik la, Ekkehardt Mueller eksplike menm bagay la: lwa seremoni yo te jwenn akonplisman yo nan Jezi, pandan lalwa moral la rete kòm lalwa libète Jak pale de li a (Jak 1:25, Jak 2:12).

Gen de pasaj nan Nouvo Testaman an moun souvan site pou di tout lalwa fini. Efezyen 2:15 pale de lalwa ak kòmandman li yo ki te an fòm règleman, ke Kris te aboli nan kò li, epi Kolosyen 2:14 rive 17 pale de yon dokiman règleman Kris te kloure sou lakwa li, ak bagay ki te sèlman yon lonbraj sa ki t ap vini. Nou konprann pasaj sa yo, menm jan ak etid Mueller la, kòm pawòl sou lwa seremoni yo ki te montre dwèt sou Kris, pa sou Dis Kòmandman yo; se yon entèpretasyon, epi nou di l kareman. Gen lòt kretyen ki li yo kòm prèv ke tout lalwa Moyiz la, ansanm ak Dis Kòmandman yo, te fini sou lakwa, epi nou respekte sensèrite yo. Men paske Jezi, Pòl ak Jak kontinye site kòmandman moral yo kòm gid pou kretyen, nou kwè lekti sa a pi byen respekte tout Ekriti a.

## Poukisa kretyen yo pa konte Dis Kòmandman yo menm jan?

Kretyen yo pa konte Dis Kòmandman yo menm jan paske tèks Egzòd 20 la pa mete nimewo devan chak kòmandman, kidonk chak tradisyon divize pawòl yo nan fason ki sanble li pi lojik pou li. Tout moun dakò gen dis pawòl, paske Bib la menm di sa (Egzòd 34:28, Detewonòm 4:13). Sa ki chanje se kote pou koupe. Jason DeRouchie, nan yon atik sou sit Logos la, dekri twa gwo fason.

Dapre opinyon ki pi gaye nan tradisyon jwif la, premye pawòl la se fraz "Mwen menm se SENYÈ a Bondye ou a" nan Egzòd 20:2, epi dezyèm nan mete ansanm "pa gen lòt dye" ak "pa fè zidòl" (vèsè 3 rive 6). Nan tradisyon katolik ak literyen an, vèsè 2 rive 6 yo fòme yon sèl premye kòmandman, epi pou yo toujou rive nan dis, yo divize dènye kòmandman sou anvi a an de. Nan tradisyon refòme, anglikan, ak òtodòks yo, premye kòmandman an se "pa gen lòt dye" (vèsè 3), dezyèm nan se "pa fè zidòl" (vèsè 4 rive 6), epi kòmandman sou anvi a rete yon sèl. Se fason sa a nou swiv nan etid sa a.

Kidonk si yon zanmi katolik di w "twazyèm kòmandman an" pou pale de Saba a, pa fè kòlè, ni pa panse li gen lòt kòmandman pase ou. Nou tou de ap pale de menm pawòl Bondye a, nou jis konte l yon lòt jan. Sa ki pi enpòtan, se pa ki nimewo nou bay chak kòmandman, men si nou kenbe tout dis yo jan Bondye te pale yo.

## Kijan pou fanmi w viv Dis Kòmandman yo chak jou?

Fanmi w ka viv Dis Kòmandman yo chak jou lè nou aprann yo ansanm, nou pale de yo nan sitiyasyon reyèl, epi nou kite lagras Bondye vini anvan règ yo. Detewonòm 6:6 rive 7 mande paran yo pale de pawòl Bondye lè yo chita lakay yo, lè yo sou wout, lè yo kouche ak lè yo leve. Se pa yon klas fòmèl, se yon konvèsasyon ki pa janm fini. Men kèk etap senp pou kòmanse.

- Aprann yo ansanm : Chak semèn, chwazi yon kòmandman, li l nan Egzòd 20 epi aprann li pa kè ak timoun yo
- Poze yon kesyon nan tab la : Mande chak moun: ki kote nou te wè kòmandman sa a jodi a, lekòl, travay, oswa sou telefòn?
- Kòmanse ak lagras : Raple timoun yo ke Bondye te libere pèp la anvan li ba yo lalwa, e li renmen yo menm lè yo fè erè
- Fè l vizib : Ekri dis yo sou yon fèy epi kole l sou frijidè a, kote tout moun pase plizyè fwa pa jou
- Fini ak lapriyè : Mande Bondye ekri lalwa li nan kè nou, pa sèlman sou papye a

Lè yon timoun fè yon erè, sèvi ak kòmandman an kòm yon pòt pou pale de padon, pa kòm yon baton pou frape. Ou ka di: "Ou konnen sa Bondye di sou manti a. Ann priye ansanm pou mande l padon, epi ann chèche kijan pou n repare sa." Konsa timoun nan aprann ke lalwa montre nou peche nou, men Jezi se sila a ki padone nou. Pa gen pi bon leson sou Dis Kòmandman yo pase yon papa oswa yon manman ki viv yo devan je pitit li.

## Kesyon moun poze

### Èske Dis Kòmandman yo te sèlman pou pèp Izrayèl la?

Non, Dis Kòmandman yo pa t sèlman pou pèp Izrayèl la, paske yo dekri prensip moral Bondye pou tout limanite. Menm anvan Sinayi, Bib la montre ke touye moun ak adiltè te deja peche devan Bondye, tankou nan istwa Kayen (Jenèz 4) ak istwa Jozèf (Jenèz 39:9). Bondye te bay pèp Izrayèl la lalwa a ekri pou lòt nasyon yo te ka wè sajès li atravè yo (Detewonòm 4:6). Nan Nouvo Testaman an, Pòl ekri pou kretyen lavil Wòm, anpil ladan yo pa t jwif, epi li toujou site kòmandman yo kòm gid pou lavi yo (Women 13:9).

### Si m kase youn nan kòmandman yo, èske Bondye ap rejte m?

Non, Bondye pa rejte moun ki kase yon kòmandman epi ki tounen vin jwenn li ak yon kè ki repanti. Bib la di si nou konfese peche nou, Bondye fidèl e jis pou l padone nou epi pou l netwaye nou (1 Jan 1:9). Lalwa montre nou kote nou tonbe, men se lagras ki leve nou. David te kase plizyè kòmandman, men lè li te repanti, li te ekri Sòm 51, youn nan pi bèl priyè padon nan Bib la.

### Ki diferans ki genyen ant Egzòd 20 ak Detewonòm 5?

Diferans prensipal ant Egzòd 20 ak Detewonòm 5 se nan rezon yo bay pou Saba a ak kèk ti mo, men se menm dis kòmandman yo. Nan Egzòd, rezon pou Saba a se kreyasyon an (Egzòd 20:11). Nan Detewonòm, Moyiz ajoute souvni delivrans lan, paske Bondye te fè pèp la soti anba esklavaj (Detewonòm 5:15). Lòd mo yo nan dènye kòmandman an chanje tou, Detewonòm mete madanm vwazen an anvan kay li (Detewonòm 5:21). De pasaj yo ansanm montre ke Bondye se tou de Kreyatè nou ak Liberatè nou.

## Kesyon pou reflechi

Ki kòmandman ou santi ki pi difisil pou ou viv semèn sa a, e poukisa ou panse se li menm? Lè ou panse a lalwa Bondye, èske ou wè l plis tankou yon lis entèdiksyon, oswa tankou yon pòtre lanmou Bondye pou ou? Ki ti chanjman ou ta ka fè lakay ou pou pitit ou yo, oswa moun ki viv avè w, aprann Dis Kòmandman yo nan yon atmosfè lajwa olye de laperèz?

## Yon pawòl ankourajman

Si ou li lis sa a epi ou santi w kondane, tande sa: Bondye pa t bay Dis Kòmandman yo pou kraze w. Menm Bondye ki te ekri yo sou wòch la, se li menm ki te voye Pitit li pou mouri pou ou, paske li konnen nou pa t ka kenbe yo pou kont nou. Jezi te viv lalwa a nèt ale nan plas ou, li te peye pou tout fwa ou te tonbe, epi kounye a li pwomèt pou l ekri lalwa li nan kè ou. Ou pa bezwen vin pafè anvan ou vin jwenn li. Vin jan ou ye a, epi kite l fè travay li nan ou, yon jou apre lòt.

## Yon lapriyè

Papa nou ki nan syèl la, mèsi paske ou pa t kite nou san chemen. Mèsi pou Dis Kòmandman ou yo, ki montre nou kijan ou ye ak kijan pou nou renmen. Nou konfese ke nou pa toujou mache ladan yo, e nou mande w padon nan non Jezi. Tanpri ekri lalwa ou nan kè nou ak nan kè pitit nou yo, pou obeyisans nou tounen yon chante lanmou pou ou. Nou priye nan non Jezi, amen.

## Pwochen etap ou

Si etid sa a louvri lòt kesyon nan tèt ou, se yon bon siy: sa vle di ou pare pou ale pi fon nan Pawòl Bondye a. Nou envite w kòmanse yon etid biblik gratis, kote ou ka poze kesyon w yo san presyon epi dekouvri sa Bib la di sou lalwa, lagras, ak Jezi nan pwòp ritm ou. Ou kapab tou vin vizite nou nan legliz Shekinah nan Alvarado, Texas, kote nou adore an Kreyòl ak an Anglè. Lekòl Saba kòmanse chak Samdi a 10:00 AM, epi sèvis adorasyon an kòmanse a 11:00 AM. N ap kontan resevwa w ak tout fanmi w.

Related: [Kòmanse yon etid biblik gratis](https://shekinahsda.org/bible-study/)

Related: [Planifye vizit ou nan legliz Shekinah](https://shekinahsda.org/kreyol/planifye-vizit/)

- Source: [19. The Law of God (Fundamental Beliefs), North American Division](https://www.nadadventist.org/beliefs/the-law-of-god/)

- Source: [The Law and the Gospel, Ekkehardt Mueller, Biblical Research Institute](https://adventistbiblicalresearch.org/articles/the-law-and-the-gospel)

- Source: [3 Ways to Number the Ten Commandments, Jason S. DeRouchie, Logos](https://www.logos.com/grow/hall-number-ten-commandments/)

- Source: [Egzòd 20, Bib Sen An (BSA), YouVersion](https://www.bible.com/bible-verses/3821/EXO.20.BSA)

- Source: [Matthew 5:17, King James Bible Online](https://www.kingjamesbibleonline.org/Matthew-5-17/)

- Source: [Matthew 22:37 to 40, KJV, Biblia](https://biblia.com/bible/kjv/Mt22.37-40)

- Source: [Ephesians 2:8 to 10, KJV, YouVersion](https://www.bible.com/el/bible/1/EPH.2.8-10.KJV)

# The Eight Laws of Health: One Small Habit a Week for the Whole Family

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/eight-laws-of-health/
Category: Health
Author: Esther Valcourt
Published: 2026-11-09

The eight laws of health, often taught as NEWSTART, are eight simple gifts from God that any family can begin practicing this week, one small habit at a time.


It is Sunday evening and the week ahead already feels crowded. Work, school pickups, groceries, and a stack of good intentions about eating better and sleeping more all compete for the same few hours. Maybe you have read about the eight laws of health and wondered whether they are a real plan or just one more list that will make you feel behind. If that sounds familiar, take a breath, because this guide was written for busy families like yours.

The eight laws of health are not a diet, a product, or a program you have to buy. They are eight simple gifts God has already placed within reach: good food, movement, water, sunlight, temperance, fresh air, rest, and trust in Him. Seventh-day Adventists have taught them for well over a century, and many churches today use the memory word NEWSTART to keep them in mind.

Below we walk through each law one at a time. For every one you will find a fact from a trusted health source, a short word from Scripture, and one small habit your family can try this week. This is general wellness education and not medical advice, so please talk with your doctor about your own health, especially before you change your activity or diet with a medical condition.

## The short answer

The eight laws of health are eight natural remedies taught by Seventh-day Adventists: nutrition, exercise, water, sunlight, temperance, fresh air, rest, and trust in God. The NEWSTART acronym spells them out letter by letter. They work best together as a daily rhythm rather than a menu, and each can begin with one small, practical habit that the whole family can share.

- 150 min : Weekly moderate activity for adults (CDC)
- 7 hours : Minimum nightly sleep for most adults (CDC)
- 90% : Share of time Americans spend indoors (EPA)

## Where do the eight laws of health come from?

The eight laws of health come from the Adventist health message, most clearly from a single sentence Ellen G. White wrote in The Ministry of Healing. In the chapter called "Natural Remedies," she listed "Pure air, sunlight, abstemiousness, rest, exercise, proper diet, the use of water, trust in divine power" and called these "the true remedies" (The Ministry of Healing, page 127). Abstemiousness is an older word for self control, which is why most modern lists call it temperance.

Many years later the Weimar Institute arranged the same eight ideas into the acronym NEWSTART, according to a health seminar outline published by Adventist Family Ministries. That outline stresses that the eight work as one package, not as separate options to pick and choose. The order of the letters is simply a memory aid, so you can start with whichever law feels easiest in your home.

| Letter | Law of health | One habit to try this week |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N | Nutrition | Fill half of supper plates with vegetables and fruit |
| E | Exercise | Take a family walk after a meal |
| W | Water | Keep a pitcher of water on the table |
| S | Sunlight | Step outside in the morning light |
| T | Temperance | Choose one habit to trim for seven days |
| A | Air | Open a window or eat outdoors once |
| R | Rest | Set a family lights out time |
| T | Trust in God | Pray together before sleep |

## Is the Adventist health message in the Bible?

The Bible does not list eight laws of health by name, but it does teach that our bodies matter to God and that daily choices can honor Him. The apostle John opened a short letter to his friend Gaius with a prayer for both body and soul. His words show that caring about someone's physical health is part of loving them as a Christian.

> "Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth." 3 John 1:2, KJV

Paul applied the same idea to the most ordinary parts of life, even our meals. He wrote that the way we eat and drink can be an act of worship, not because food saves us, but because everything we do can be done for God. In context he was answering questions about food and conscience, yet his closing principle reaches every part of daily life.

> "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God." 1 Corinthians 10:31, KJV

The church's Fundamental Belief 22, Christian Behavior, puts it this way: "because our bodies are the temples of the Holy Spirit, we are to care for them intelligently." The same belief says that "along with adequate exercise and rest, we are to adopt the most healthful diet possible." The eight laws are one practical way of living out that teaching, while the Bible itself remains our authority and grace, not health habits, remains the ground of our salvation.

## N is for nutrition: what does a healthy plate look like?

A healthy plate is mostly plants, and the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health suggests making half your plate vegetables and fruits, a quarter whole grains, and a quarter healthy protein. Its Healthy Eating Plate also advises drinking water and skipping sugary drinks. Genesis 1:29 shows that the first diet God gave was made of seed bearing plants and fruit, which is one reason many Seventh-day Adventists choose plant based meals today.

In a Haitian kitchen this already feels familiar. A plate of diri ak pwa with a generous spoon of legim and a bright side of sliced avocado or cabbage moves closer to the Harvard pattern, especially when brown rice replaces some of the white and the vegetables get the most room. Your habit this week is simple: at supper, let vegetables and fruit cover half of every plate before anything else goes on it.

Related: [Eating for Life: Simple Plant Based Meals from Our Kitchen](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/eating-for-life-simple-plant-based-meals-from-our-kitchen/)

## E is for exercise: how much activity do you really need?

Most adults need at least 150 minutes of moderate activity each week, such as brisk walking, plus muscle strengthening activities on at least 2 days, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The CDC recommends 60 minutes or more of moderate to vigorous activity every day for children and teens ages 6 to 17. For adults living with a chronic condition or disability, the CDC gives the same 150 minute weekly target, and the page adds that anyone unable to meet the recommendations should be as active as they can.

That 150 minutes can be as gentle as 30 minutes on 5 days, and it does not require a gym. Texas evenings in the cooler months are perfect for a walk around the block after supper, with children on bikes and grandparents setting the pace. Your habit this week is one family walk after a meal, and if you have heart trouble, joint pain, or another health concern, check with your doctor first about what pace is right for you.

Related: [Walk With Me: Starting a Sabbath Afternoon Walking Group](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/walk-with-me-starting-a-sabbath-afternoon-walking-group/)

## W is for water: how much water should you drink a day?

Mayo Clinic says the average healthy adult gets enough water with about 11.5 to 15.5 cups of total fluid a day, and that count includes all drinks plus the water in food. Mayo Clinic notes that food supplies about 20 percent of the water we need. A practical check is the color of your urine: colorless or light yellow usually means you are drinking enough.

Needs go up when you sweat, and Mayo Clinic points out that hot or humid weather calls for more fluid than usual. Anyone who has worked a yard in a North Texas summer knows that feeling well. Your habit this week is to set a pitcher of cold dlo on the table at every meal, so that water is the easiest drink to reach for.

Related: [Water First: Small Habits for Big Energy](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/water-first-small-habits-for-big-energy/)

## S is for sunlight: why does morning light matter?

Morning light matters because daylight helps set the body clock that tells us when to wake and when to sleep. Among its tips for healthy sleep, the CDC recommends getting daylight, especially earlier in the day, such as during a morning or lunchtime walk. A short walk outside in the morning can practice two laws at once, sunlight and exercise.

Light was the first thing God spoke into creation, and He called it good (Genesis 1:3 to 4). As the days shorten in November, the gift of daylight is easy to miss between an early commute and an evening indoors. Your habit this week is to step outside for a few minutes each morning, even just to drink a glass of water on the porch before the day begins.

Related: [Sunlight in the Shorter Days: Vitamin D, Mood, and God's Gift of Light](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/sunlight-in-the-shorter-days-vitamin-d-and-mood/)

## T is for temperance: what does temperance mean today?

Temperance means using good things in balance and avoiding what harms us. Fundamental Belief 22 teaches that because alcoholic beverages, tobacco, and the irresponsible use of drugs and narcotics harm the body, Christians are to abstain from them. Temperance also reaches into everyday life, from how much sugar we eat to how many hours we spend on a screen.

Paul compared the Christian life to an athlete in training who keeps every appetite under control for the sake of a prize. In the verse just before, he asks his readers to picture runners in a race where only one receives the prize (1 Corinthians 9:24). Then he points out that every competitor practices self control.

> "And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible." 1 Corinthians 9:25, KJV

Temperance is not about earning God's favor, and it is never about shame. It is a fruit of the Spirit that grows as we walk with Christ (Galatians 5:22 to 23). Your habit this week is to pick one thing as a family to trim for seven days, such as soda at supper or phones at the table, and talk together about how it felt.

**Small ways to practice temperance at home**
- Serve water instead of sugary drinks
- Keep phones away from the table
- Stop eating when comfortably full
- Balance work with real rest

## A is for air: is indoor air really that different?

Indoor air can be more polluted than the air outside, and the Environmental Protection Agency reports that concentrations of some pollutants are often 2 to 5 times higher indoors than typical outdoor levels. The EPA also notes that Americans, on average, spend approximately 90 percent of their time indoors. That makes fresh air one of the most overlooked of the eight natural remedies.

Scripture tells us that God formed the first man and breathed into him the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). Every breath we take is still a gift from Him. Your habit this week is to open a window for a while each day when the weather allows, or carry supper out to the back porch on a mild autumn evening and enjoy the Texas sky together.

## R is for rest: how many hours of sleep do you need?

Most adults need at least 7 hours of sleep each night, and children and teens need more, according to the CDC. The CDC suggests keeping the same bedtime and wake time every day, including weekends, and limiting artificial light from screens in the hours before bed. It also recommends staying active during the day but not exercising within a few hours of bedtime, and working with your health care team on anything that keeps getting in the way of good sleep.

God built rest into the rhythm of creation, both in each night and in the weekly Sabbath. Jesus Himself invited His tired disciples to come apart and rest a while (Mark 6:31). Your habit this week is a family lights out time, with screens off a little earlier than usual so that everyone, parents included, can wind down.

Related: [The Gift of Rest: Why Sleep Is Part of Our Worship](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/the-gift-of-rest-why-sleep-is-part-of-our-worship/)

## T is for trust in God: can faith really support health?

Trust in God is the eighth law because worry and fear weigh on the whole person, and Scripture invites us to bring them to Him. Ellen White listed "trust in divine power" among the true remedies, and the Bible connects a steady mind with a deep peace. The prophet Isaiah put that promise into a single verse.

> "Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee." Isaiah 26:3, KJV

Trusting God does not mean ignoring symptoms or refusing treatment. It means we do our part, seek wise care, and then rest in the One who holds tomorrow. If anxiety or sadness feels heavy for many days, please reach out to a health professional, because asking for help is an act of wisdom, not a lack of faith. Your habit this week is to end each day with a short family prayer, naming one worry and one blessing aloud.

Related: [Stress Less: Trusting God With Your Worries](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/stress-less-trusting-god-with-your-worries/)

## How can a family start NEWSTART health without feeling overwhelmed?

The easiest way to start is to pick one law, practice one small habit for a week, and add another only when the first feels natural. Trying to change everything on Monday can leave a family discouraged by Thursday. Small steps practiced together tend to last longer than big promises, and the five steps below keep the process simple.

- Choose one law : Let each family member vote on where to begin
- Name one habit : Keep it small enough to do every day
- Pray about it : Ask God for strength and patience
- Review on Friday : Talk at supper about what worked
- Add the next law : Build one healthy lifestyle habit at a time

## Questions people ask

### What are the 8 natural remedies?

The 8 natural remedies are nutrition, exercise, water, sunlight, temperance, fresh air, rest, and trust in God. Ellen G. White listed them in The Ministry of Healing as pure air, sunlight, abstemiousness, rest, exercise, proper diet, the use of water, and trust in divine power. Seventh-day Adventists often call them the eight laws of health. They describe a whole way of living rather than a single treatment.

### What does NEWSTART stand for?

NEWSTART stands for Nutrition, Exercise, Water, Sunshine, Temperance, Air, Rest, and Trust in God. According to Adventist Family Ministries, the acronym was developed at the Weimar Institute as a simple way to remember the eight natural remedies. The letters make the list easy to teach to children and to share in a church health class. The ideas themselves are much older than the acronym.

### Are the eight laws of health only for Seventh-day Adventists?

No, the eight laws of health are useful for anyone, whatever church they attend or whether they attend at all. Much of what they teach, such as eating more vegetables, moving every day, drinking water, and getting enough sleep, lines up with guidance from groups like the CDC and the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. What Seventh-day Adventists add is the conviction that caring for the body is part of honoring the God who made it.

### Do natural remedies replace medicine?

No, natural remedies do not replace medicine, and they should never be a reason to skip a doctor's visit or stop a prescribed treatment. The eight laws describe healthy daily living that supports the body and can work alongside good medical care. God often works through doctors, nurses, and medicine, and there is no conflict between prayer and good care. If you have a health condition, talk with your doctor before making major changes to your diet or activity.

## Reflection questions

Which of the eight laws of health comes most naturally to your family, and which one feels the hardest right now? What is one small habit you could begin this week that would make room for God in your ordinary routine? How might your example of rest, balance, and trust encourage someone else in your home or church?

## A word of encouragement

You do not have to master all eight laws to please God, because His love for you does not depend on your step count or your plate. He invites you to receive these gifts one at a time, with patience and grace. Every glass of water, every evening walk, and every quiet prayer is a small yes to the life He offers.

Some weeks will go well and some will not, and that is part of being human. When you stumble, simply begin again the next morning. His mercies are new every morning (Lamentations 3:22 to 23), and so is your chance to care for the body He gave you.

## A prayer

Loving Father, thank You for food, water, sunlight, fresh air, and rest, and thank You most of all for the peace we find in You. Teach our family to care for these bodies with wisdom and gratitude, one small step at a time. When we feel tired or discouraged, remind us that our strength comes from You. In Jesus' name, Amen.

The best way to see these habits in action is to share them with a church family. # Ancient Empires and Prophecy: The Daniel 2 Timeline Decoded

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/daniel-2-prophecy-explained/
Category: Bible Answers
Author: Isaac Whitman
Published: 2026-11-02

Daniel 2 traces Babylon, Medo Persia, Greece, Rome, and the divided kingdoms to the stone, God's everlasting kingdom set up at the return of Christ, with a dated timeline and a fair look at other readings.


You have just finished a documentary about the fall of Rome when you open your Bible to Daniel and meet a giant statue made of gold, silver, brass, iron, and clay. Someone in your Bible study group says the whole of world history is in this one chapter. Someone else says it is only about the ancient world. So you search for Daniel 2 prophecy explained, and you find charts, confident voices, and a lot of disagreement.

That confusion is understandable, because this chapter sits where Scripture meets history. Some parts of it are stated plainly in the text, and other parts are identified by interpretation, and those two things deserve to be kept apart. We can read what Daniel says, check the dates of the empires, and listen fairly to Christians who read the chapter differently.

This article is meant to be a study guide you can use with your Bible open. It reads the prophecy the historicist way, which means seeing it unfold in order through real history from Daniel's day to the return of Jesus. Above all, it follows the chapter to the place it ends, which is not with an empire but with a kingdom that will never fall.

## The short answer

Daniel 2 is a prophecy of world history told through one statue. The gold head is Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon, and this article reads the silver, brass, and iron as Medo Persia, Greece, and Rome, followed by divided kingdoms in the iron and clay. The stone cut out without hands is God's everlasting kingdom, set up when Christ returns. Daniel gives no date for that day.

Only one of those earthly kingdoms is named by the chapter itself, and that matters. Daniel tells the king, "Thou art this head of gold" (Daniel 2:38, KJV), but he does not name the kingdoms that come after. Later chapters of Daniel help identify Medo Persia and Greece, and Rome is identified by interpretation, using the order of history and the shape of the prophecy. We will show each step so you can weigh it for yourself.

- 1 : Kingdom Daniel 2 directly identifies
- 4 : Kingdoms before the stone
- 0 : Dates given for the stone's coming

## What was Nebuchadnezzar's statue dream?

Daniel 2 opens "in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar" (Daniel 2:1, KJV), with the king of Babylon troubled by a dream he refuses to describe. He demands that his wise men tell him both the dream and its meaning, and when they say no one on earth can do that, he orders them killed (Daniel 2:2 to 13). Daniel, a young Jewish captive, asks for time and turns to prayer with his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah (Daniel 2:16 to 18). God then reveals the secret to him in a night vision (Daniel 2:19).

Daniel gives God the credit before he says a word about the dream. He tells the king, "But there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days" (Daniel 2:28, KJV). Then he describes what the king saw, a great image standing in front of him.

> "This image's head was of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver, his belly and his thighs of brass, His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay." Daniel 2:32 to 33, KJV

Then the scene changes without warning. A stone "was cut out without hands" and strikes the image on its feet, and the whole statue collapses into something like chaff on a threshing floor (Daniel 2:34 to 35, KJV). The wind carries it away so that "no place was found for them" and the stone becomes a great mountain that "filled the whole earth" (Daniel 2:35, KJV). Daniel then tells the king the meaning, and he closes with a strong assurance: "the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure" (Daniel 2:45, KJV).

## Who are the four kingdoms of Daniel?

The historicist reading identifies the four kingdoms of Daniel as Babylon, Medo Persia, Greece, and Rome, followed by the divided kingdoms that came out of Rome. Babylon is identified in the chapter itself, while the others rest on interpretation supported by later chapters and by the order of history. The Biblical Research Institute, in its study of Daniel 2, sets out this same sequence with similar dates. The table below gives it at a glance, and the sections after it explain the reasoning.

| Part of the image | Kingdom | Approximate dates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Head of gold | Babylon (identified in Daniel 2:38) | About 605 to 539 BC |
| Breast and arms of silver | Medo Persia (by interpretation, see Daniel 5:28) | 539 to 331 BC |
| Belly and thighs of brass | Greece (by interpretation, see Daniel 8:21) | 331 to 168 BC |
| Legs of iron | Rome (by interpretation) | 168 BC to AD 476 |
| Feet of iron and clay | Divided kingdoms (by interpretation) | After AD 476 |
| The stone | God's everlasting kingdom (Daniel 2:44) | At the return of Christ (by interpretation), date unknown |

### Babylon: the head of gold

Babylon is the one clear starting point, because Daniel speaks directly to its king. Encyclopaedia Britannica dates the reign of Nebuchadnezzar to about 605 to 561 BC, and it describes Babylon under him as a major imperial power. Daniel tells him that the God of heaven gave him his kingdom (Daniel 2:37 to 38). The gold was an honor, but it was also a reminder that even this ruler held power only by God's permission, for it is God who "removeth kings, and setteth up kings" (Daniel 2:21, KJV).

### Medo Persia: the silver

Daniel 2 says only, "And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee" (Daniel 2:39, KJV), so the chapter does not name this power. Daniel 5 fills in the gap. On the night Babylon falls, the message to Belshazzar is, "Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians" (Daniel 5:28, KJV), and that same night he is slain (Daniel 5:30). Britannica records that the Persians under Cyrus II attacked in 539 BC and that the capital fell almost without resistance.

### Greece: the brass

The third kingdom is called "another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth" (Daniel 2:39, KJV), and again it is not named in this chapter. Daniel 8 gives us the help we need with a vision of a ram and a goat, in which the ram is overthrown. The angel explains, "The ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia" (Daniel 8:20, KJV), and "the rough goat is the king of Grecia" (Daniel 8:21, KJV). History matches that order, because the Battle of Gaugamela, between Alexander the Great and Darius III of Persia, was fought on October 1, 331 BC, and it decided the fate of the Persian empire.

### Why is Rome identified as the fourth kingdom?

Rome is identified as the fourth kingdom because it is the power that followed Greece, and because it fits the iron that "breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things" (Daniel 2:40, KJV). Daniel never uses the name Rome, so this is an interpretation, and it should be held as one. Still, the pieces fit well. Britannica dates the Battle of Pydna to June 22, 168 BC, when Rome defeated King Perseus of Macedonia, ended the Macedonian monarchy, and split its territory into four republics.

The New Testament opens with Rome in exactly the place this reading expects. Luke writes that "there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed" (Luke 2:1, KJV), so the world of Jesus' birth was a Roman world. This identification is also an old one. Jerome, the ancient Bible translator, named the four kingdoms of Daniel 2 in his commentary as the Babylonians, the Medes and Persians, the Macedonians, and the Romans, and many Christian interpreters since have kept the same order.

### What do the iron and clay feet mean?

The iron and clay feet show a fourth kingdom that loses its unity without losing all of its strength. Daniel says that "the kingdom shall be divided" (Daniel 2:41, KJV), that it "shall be partly strong, and partly broken" (Daniel 2:42, KJV), and that its parts "shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay" (Daniel 2:43, KJV). This article reads that as the breakup of Rome in the West. Britannica describes Visigoths in Spain, Vandals at Carthage, Ostrogoths at Ravenna, Franks across the Rhine, and Angles and Saxons in Britain, and it dates the end of the Western empire to AD 476, when Odoacer deposed the emperor Romulus Augustulus.

Dates like these are markers, not walls, and honesty requires saying so. Pydna did not place every Greek speaking land under Rome in a single day, and Rome's eastern empire survived until 1453. What the reading sees is the broad movement of history, in which no single power has again held the place Rome held in the West. As the Biblical Research Institute puts it, the iron and clay picture a divided kingdom and no longer a world empire.

**Reading the text honestly**
- Stated in Daniel 2: the head of gold is Nebuchadnezzar
- Stated in Daniel 2: God sets up a kingdom that stands for ever
- Helped by Daniel 5 and 8: Medo Persia and Greece
- By interpretation: Rome and the divided kingdoms
- Not stated anywhere: the date of Christ's return

## How does the Daniel 2 timeline line up with history?

The Daniel 2 timeline lines up with history as a sequence of empires, with four turning points that can be dated from ordinary historical sources. The prophecy itself gives no years at all, so the dates below come from historians and not from the Bible. What Scripture supplies is the order and the ending. This is why the study of Bible prophecy history is worth the effort, because the past gives us reason to trust what is still to come.

- About 605 BC: Nebuchadnezzar begins to reign: Daniel 2:1 places the dream in his second year.

- 539 BC: Babylon falls: Cyrus II and the Persians take the capital.

- 331 BC: Battle of Gaugamela: Alexander defeats Darius III of Persia.

- 168 BC: Battle of Pydna: Rome ends the Macedonian monarchy.

- AD 476: Western empire ends: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus.

- After AD 476: Divided kingdoms: Partly strong and partly broken, as Daniel 2:42 says.

- Date unknown: The stone strikes: Christ returns and God's kingdom stands for ever.

## How do other Christians read Daniel 2?

Sincere readers disagree about this chapter, and it is worth hearing them in their own terms. The three other readings most people will meet are the critical view that ends with Greece, the amillennial view that sees the stone in the church, and the futurist view of a revived Roman Empire. Each one takes something in the chapter seriously. Here is a summary, followed by a fair description of each and the reasons this article reads the text differently.

| Reading | Fourth kingdom | The stone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Historicist (this article) | Rome, then divided kingdoms | God's kingdom set up at Christ's return |
| Critical | Greek rule in the Seleucid and Ptolemaic kingdoms | God's rule expected in that era |
| Amillennial | Usually Rome | Christ's kingdom begun at His first coming and growing through the church |
| Futurist | Rome, with a future revived phase | Christ's kingdom after His return |

### Why do some scholars say the fourth kingdom is Greece?

Many modern scholars read the sequence as Babylon, Media, Persia, and Greek rule, with Antiochus IV as the little horn of Daniel 7. The notes of the New American Bible, Revised Edition, for example, name the Babylonian, Median, Persian, and Hellenistic kingdoms, and they say the divided Greek kingdoms of the Ptolemies and Seleucids tried in vain to restore unity by war and intermarriage. In this view the book speaks to Jewish believers who suffered under Antiochus in the second century BC. The idea is not only a modern one, since Jerome reports that the ancient critic Porphyry tied the book to the time of Antiochus. These scholars are taking the book's historical setting seriously, and readers can learn a great deal from their work.

The difficulty for this reading is the way Daniel itself treats the Medes and Persians. Daniel 5:28 gives Babylon to both peoples together, Daniel 6:8 speaks of one "law of the Medes and Persians" (KJV), and Daniel 8:20 pictures them as one ram with two horns. If they are one power in the book, there is no separate Median kingdom to fill the second place, and Greece falls into third place, as Daniel 8 suggests. That leaves the fourth place for a power that came after Greece.

### Is the stone the church?

Many Christians, including those who hold the amillennial view, understand the stone as the kingdom of Christ that began at His first coming and has been growing ever since. Jason Jackson of Christian Courier, for example, connects Daniel 2:44 with the beginning of the church in Acts 2 and sees a spiritual conquest that wins people freely and reaches its goal when the Lord returns. Parables seem to support this picture, since Jesus said, "The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed" and "like unto leaven" (Matthew 13:31 and 33, KJV). This reading rightly insists that Jesus reigns now and that His kingdom is not built by force. He told Pilate, "My kingdom is not of this world" (John 18:36, KJV).

There is real truth here, and this article gladly affirms it. Christ rules today in the hearts of those who trust Him, in what Christians have often called the kingdom of grace. But the stone in Daniel 2 does something different from a seed or leaven. It does not slowly change the image from within; it strikes the feet, the image is "broken to pieces together," and only then does the stone become a mountain (Daniel 2:35, KJV). The kingdoms of this world did not disappear at Pentecost, so this article understands the stone as the kingdom of glory that comes with the return of Christ.

### Is the fourth kingdom a revived Roman Empire?

Futurist readers agree that Rome is the fourth kingdom, but many divide it into two phases. The legs are ancient Rome, and the feet and toes are a revived Roman Empire still to come, often linked with the ten horns of Daniel 7 and with the final years before Christ's return. An article from Harvest House Publishers on the four kingdoms sets out this view. This reading deserves credit for keeping the stone's blow in the future and for expecting a real, personal coming of Christ, and on those points this article stands with it.

The main question is one of continuity. In the statue the iron runs straight from the legs into the feet with no gap, so this article reads the divided state as following directly from Rome's fall and continuing through the centuries since. The text also does not number the toes, so we will not attempt a list of ten nations, and we do not need to guess at future alliances. Daniel 2 gives us the shape of history and its ending, and that is enough.

## What does the stone cut without hands mean?

The stone cut without hands is God's everlasting kingdom, which He sets up Himself and which replaces every human kingdom. The words "without hands" show that no army, government, or human movement produces it. Daniel explains it in the clearest verse of the chapter.

> "And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever." Daniel 2:44, KJV

Three things in that verse carry the argument. The kingdom comes from "the God of heaven," it passes to no successor as every other kingdom on the statue did, and it brings all the others to an end. Daniel 7 runs along the same track, with "the fourth kingdom upon earth" (Daniel 7:23, KJV) giving way to what the chapter calls "an everlasting kingdom" (Daniel 7:27, KJV). Reading the stone as the second coming of Christ is an interpretation, but it fits how the New Testament speaks of His return. Jesus said, "When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory" (Matthew 25:31, KJV).

Jesus also connected Himself with stone language when He warned, "Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder" (Luke 20:18, KJV). Revelation describes the same turning of the ages: "The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever" (Revelation 11:15, KJV). That return will be open to all, for "every eye shall see him" (Revelation 1:7, KJV). The Biblical Research Institute likewise treats the stone as an image of God or Jesus, and it looks to His return as the time He establishes His eternal kingdom. That is why the prayer Jesus taught still fits this chapter: "Thy kingdom come" (Matthew 6:10, KJV).

### When does the mountain fill the whole earth?

Daniel 2 gives the order, the stone first and then the mountain, but it does not say how much time lies between them. It also never mentions the thousand years, so what follows is interpretation that compares Scripture with Scripture. Jesus promised, "I will come again, and receive you unto myself" (John 14:3, KJV), and Paul says that the risen dead and the living believers will meet Him together, "and so shall we ever be with the Lord" (1 Thessalonians 4:17, KJV). Revelation then says the saints "lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years" (Revelation 20:4, KJV). This article understands that reign as taking place in heaven, while the earth lies empty.

At the close of the thousand years, John sees "the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven" (Revelation 21:2, KJV), and "a new earth" (Revelation 21:1, KJV) where God "will dwell with them" (Revelation 21:3, KJV). Here this article sees the mountain reach its full meaning, a kingdom that fills an earth made new. Many Christians, including most futurists, expect Christ to reign on the present earth during the thousand years, and they hold that view sincerely from their own reading of Revelation 20. All of these readers can agree on the ending Daniel gives, a kingdom that will "stand for ever" (Daniel 2:44, KJV).

Related: [What Does the Bible Say About the Second Coming of Jesus?](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/what-does-the-bible-say-about-the-second-coming-of-jesus/)

## Can Daniel 2 tell us when Jesus will return?

No, Daniel 2 does not tell us when Jesus will return, and no one should use it to set a date. The chapter gives an order of kingdoms and an ending, not a calendar. Jesus Himself said, "But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only" (Matthew 24:36, KJV). On this reading we live in the time of the feet, the last stage before the stone, so we believe His coming is near without knowing which day the story ends. That is why Jesus said, "Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come" (Matthew 24:42, KJV).

## How can you study Daniel 2 for yourself?

You can study Daniel 2 well by reading the text first and adding interpretation only after that. The steps below keep what the chapter says apart from what we conclude about it, which is the most useful habit in all prophecy study. A slow reading with an open Bible will teach you more than any chart.

- Read the chapter : All 49 verses in one sitting
- Mark what is stated : Underline what the text itself explains
- Follow the links : Read Daniel 5, 7, and 8
- Check the history : Compare dates in a good encyclopedia
- End with Jesus : Ask what this says about His kingdom

## Questions people ask

### What is the main message of Daniel 2?

The main message of Daniel 2 is that God rules over history and that His kingdom will outlast every human power. The chapter is less a puzzle about empires than a statement about who is truly in charge. Daniel's own prayer says it best when he praises the God who removes kings and sets up kings (Daniel 2:21).

### Does the Bible say the toes represent ten kingdoms?

No, Daniel 2 mentions toes but never gives them a number. Daniel 7:24 does speak of ten horns, and many interpreters have connected the two passages, which is understandable. Still, that connection is an interpretation and does not come from Daniel 2 itself. This article describes the feet simply as divided kingdoms, because that is what the chapter says.

### Why does the image go from gold down to clay?

The image moves from gold to clay in the order the kingdoms appear, and each metal is a different kind of symbol. Daniel calls the second kingdom "inferior" (Daniel 2:39, KJV), and he describes the iron as strong and the clay as weak, but he never explains every detail of the materials. It is wise not to press beyond what he says. The clearest lesson is that human power, however impressive, ends in brittleness, while the stone endures.

### Did Daniel 2 come true?

Believers see Daniel 2 as fulfilled so far in the rise and fall of the empires, with the stone still to come. Babylon did fall, Persia did follow, Greece did overtake Persia, and Rome did rise and then divide in the West, and those events can be dated from ordinary history. Whether those events are what Daniel foresaw is a matter of faith and interpretation, and scholars disagree about it. The final part of the prophecy is a promise, and it remains ahead of us.

## Reflection questions

When you look at the news, what would change if you truly believed that God "removeth kings, and setteth up kings"? Which kingdom are you building your hopes on today, one that will fade like the metals of the image, or the one that will stand for ever? How could you pray "Thy kingdom come" this week in a way that shapes how you treat the people around you?

## A word of encouragement

If you opened this chapter feeling small in front of big events, you are in good company. Daniel was a captive in a foreign land, standing before the most powerful king of his day, and he was not afraid to say that there is a God in heaven. Jesus, who was born under one of those empires, is the one the Christian hope rests on. Titus calls it "that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ" (Titus 2:13, KJV), and nothing in history has been able to take that hope away.

## A prayer

Father in heaven, You reveal secrets, You rule over the rise and fall of nations, and You know the day we do not know. Keep us from fear when the world shakes, and keep us from pride when we think we understand. Teach us to read Your Word with honest and humble hearts. Thank You for Jesus, the King whose kingdom will never end, and help us to live ready for His coming. Amen.

## Your next step

If this chapter has stirred questions, the best next step is to keep reading with someone beside you. Shekinah church in Alvarado, Texas offers free Bible studies, and you can begin with whatever you are wondering about, whether that is Daniel, the return of Jesus, or how to start reading Scripture at all. No background is needed, and your questions are welcome. Start a free Bible study today, and let the God who revealed this dream to Daniel speak to you through His Word.
